description: Table 9 is a single nine-row data table (one header row plus eight data rows) titled "Theoretical calculation results of various strengthening effects in the austenite of low-density steels". Column headers are: Samples, Aging states, σd [MPa], σg [MPa], σp [MPa] and σoro [MPa]. Rows are grouped into two steel families, "0.02Nb steels" and "0.04Nb steels", each with four aging states: as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h. For 0.02Nb steels the σd/σg/σp/σoro values are 113.1/90.8/59.4/4.9 (as-cast), 87.4/90.6/180.6/4.3, 70.8/89.9/230.0/4.2 and 40.2/88.6/274.8/4.7 MPa. For 0.04Nb steels they are 169.8/128.4/53.1/6.2, 129.0/127.0/127.4/4.7, 106.1/125.8/156.8/4.6 and 98.9/125.6/230.2/4.8 MPa. With increasing aging temperature σd falls monotonically while σp rises monotonically in both steels; σg stays nearly constant (88.6-90.8 MPa for 0.02Nb, 125.6-128.4 MPa for 0.04Nb) and σoro stays small (4.2-6.2 MPa). The 0.04Nb steels show consistently higher σd and σg than the 0.02Nb steels, whereas the 0.02Nb steel reaches the larger σp at the highest aging temperature. The table quantifies how aging trades dislocation strengthening for precipitation strengthening at nearly constant grain-boundary and Orowan contributions.

subfigures.description: Single tabular panel listing eight sample/aging conditions (0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, as-cast plus 723/773/823 K for 3 h) against four strengthening contributions in MPa: sigma_d, sigma_g, sigma_p and sigma_oro. All cells are legible and agree with the caption.

observations.observation: Table 9 reports four theoretical strengthening contributions in austenite, column-headed sigma_d, sigma_g, sigma_p and sigma_oro, all in MPa.
Two steel groups are tabulated, '0.02Nb steels' and '0.04Nb steels', each with aging states as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h.
In 0.02Nb steels, sigma_d decreases with aging temperature from 113.1 MPa (as-cast) to 87.4, 70.8 and 40.2 MPa at 723, 773 and 823 K/3 h.
In 0.02Nb steels, sigma_p increases with aging temperature from 59.4 MPa (as-cast) to 180.6, 230.0 and 274.8 MPa at 723, 773 and 823 K/3 h.
In 0.04Nb steels, sigma_d decreases with aging temperature from 169.8 MPa (as-cast) to 129.0, 106.1 and 98.9 MPa, while sigma_p increases from 53.1 MPa to 127.4, 156.8 and 230.2 MPa.
sigma_g is nearly invariant with aging state: 90.8/90.6/89.9/88.6 MPa for 0.02Nb steels and 128.4/127.0/125.8/125.6 MPa for 0.04Nb steels.
sigma_oro is the smallest contribution in every row, ranging only from 4.2 to 6.2 MPa.
The 0.04Nb steels have higher sigma_d and higher sigma_g than the 0.02Nb steels in every listed aging state; the maximum sigma_p (274.8 MPa) belongs to the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K/3 h.
The caption states the table gives theoretical calculation results of various strengthening effects in the austenite of low-density steels.
